correctness.rationale: Equation (4) expands \(\sum N_i^2\) into the pair-collision count. Conditional on one pair collision, the global separable score has exactly one size-\(B+2\) box and \(m-1\) size-\(B\) boxes, while unconditional occupancies use an independent Bin(2,p) increment; their difference is \(q\mathbb E\Delta^2f(B)\). The binomial ratios derive the finite quadratic sign polynomial, whose discriminant and positive endpoints give two roots in (0,n). Singleton and doubleton thresholds follow direct substitution, integral roots reduce to the negative Pell equation with standard descent, and the Poisson limit follows bounded pointwise convergence. Full-space exact-rational enumeration across 378 coordinate cases plus 2 nonlinear score functions per included parameter pair corroborated all calculations; no experiment is used to prove infinite scope.

value.rationale: Pearson uniformity test and frequency-of-frequencies (particularly empty cells, singletons and doubletons) are central independent diagnostics for sparse categorical data. The exact all-frequency covariance phase diagram characterizes where they reinforce or oppose each other without approximations, and the doubleton zero threshold produces a natural infinite arithmetic classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The universal discrete-curvature identity also explains the structural mechanism and Poisson-Charlier scaling. Scope avoids unproved test-power or association assertions.
